opportunities.funder: Carnegie Trust for the Universities of Scotland
opportunities.title: Undergraduate Tuition Fee Grants

amount.raw: Our grants cover the cost of tuition fees, up to £1,820 per year for a full-time degree course.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Individuals from low-income households who are ordinarily resident in Scotland and enrolled (or holding an unconditional offer) on an undergraduate degree course at an eligible Scottish Higher Education Institution, and who are not eligible for government tuition fee funding (e.g. SAAS). Includes support for some second-degree reskilling in skills-shortage areas.
opportunities.summary: Grants covering the cost of undergraduate tuition fees (up to £1,820 per year) for students from low-income households in Scotland who are ineligible for government tuition fee support. The application portal is open from 1 June 2026 to 5pm 1 December 2026 for academic year 2026-27.

opportunities.funder: Carnegie Trust for the Universities of Scotland
opportunities.title: Carnegie-Morgan Scholarship

amount.raw: Full tuition fees for the MSc in Biodiversity and Taxonomy of Plants plus an additional living-cost bursary of £1,200.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Scottish-domiciled students from low-income households, ordinarily resident in Scotland, who have been accepted onto the MSc Biodiversity and Taxonomy of Plants (delivered by Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh and the University of Edinburgh), studying part-time or full-time; must not already hold a postgraduate degree.
opportunities.summary: A scholarship, developed in partnership with the Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh, covering full tuition fees and a £1,200 living-cost bursary for the MSc in Biodiversity and Taxonomy of Plants, to widen participation in postgraduate plant science and support Scotland's net-zero and biodiversity goals.
